ESCWR team brings homecoming safety lessons to Mentor, Lake Catholic students
ESCWR's Student Wellness and Prevention Services team visited Mentor High School and Lake Catholic High School to promote safe decisions during homecoming season.
The Educational Service Center of the Western Reserve's Student Wellness and Prevention Services team, representing the Rise Above: Lake and Geauga Drug Free Communities Coalition, recently visited Mentor High School and Lake Catholic High School to share prevention messages with students during homecoming season, according to ESCWR. The visits were announced by ESCWR on Thursday, Oct. 8.
At Mentor High School, the team joined the Lake County Safe Communities Coalition as part of the school's Homecoming Blitz festivities, according to ESCWR.
Through interactive activities, hands-on games, educational materials, and giveaways, students explored the risks associated with impaired and distracted driving, the district said. Students also experienced simulated impairment while navigating pedal karts, playing basketball, and completing other activities while wearing impairment goggles, according to ESCWR.
Students were reminded to buckle up, put their phones down, never drive impaired, and always plan for a safe ride home, ESCWR said.
ESCWR thanked Mentor High School and Lake Catholic High School for welcoming the team and helping students understand that safe decision-making matters during homecoming and every time they get behind the wheel, according to the organization.
ESCWR said those interested in partnering with the Student Wellness and Prevention Services team to bring prevention education and activities to a school or community can contact the team by email.
Source: Educational Service Center of the Western Reserve, https://www.escwr.org/apps/news/article/2241025?categoryId=25265
